title: I can't assign numpad * and  numpad + in the keyboard shortcuts editor
author: CarlosGtrz
summary: Keyboard Manager appears to lose numpad operator identity in the new shortcut editor because the editor round-trips display names back into key codes and `*`/`+` are not disambiguated from the main keyboard characters.

judgment.rationale: The issue is reproducible from the public report, and the current editor code shows a concrete round-trip ambiguity between display names and virtual-key identities for numpad operator keys.
evidence: The reporter says Alt+8 -> numpad * and Alt+= -> numpad + worked in earlier builds but now emit regular * and + in 0.100.2.
KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Pages/MainPage.xaml.cs converts chosen key names back to stored codes through GetKeyCodeFromName before saving a shortcut mapping.
src/common/interop/keyboard_layout.cpp gives explicit numpad-only names to VK_DIVIDE, VK_DECIMAL, and numpad-origin navigation keys, but not to VK_MULTIPLY or VK_ADD.
src/common/interop/keyboard_layout.cpp implements LayoutMap::GetKeyFromName() as a first-match scan over display names, so duplicate labels resolve to whichever key appears first in the list.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the layout-map round-trip fix so the shortcut editor stores and redisplays numpad operator keys as distinct virtual keys.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing linked fix attempt covers this regression, and the current editor/display-name path points to a concrete PowerToys code change.

proposed_fixes.title: Disambiguate numpad operator keys in the editor key map
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The new shortcut editor persists selected keys by display name and converts them back with LayoutMap::GetKeyFromName(), but VK_MULTIPLY and VK_ADD currently reuse the plain character labels "*" and "+". That makes the round-trip ambiguous and lets the editor save the main-keyboard character key instead of the numpad operator virtual key.
plan: Give VK_MULTIPLY and VK_ADD unique user-facing names in the shared layout map, alongside the existing "/ (Numpad)" and ". (Numpad)" entries.
Keep dropdown capture and save logic using display names, but make the name-to-key round trip unique for shortcut targets.
Add focused regression coverage that enumerates the key list, resolves the saved names back to VKs, and verifies numpad operator mappings survive save/reload.
verification: Create shortcut remaps for Alt+8 -> * (Numpad) and Alt+= -> + (Numpad), save them, reopen the editor, and confirm the same numpad targets are still shown.
Use the saved remaps in a target app and confirm they emit VK_MULTIPLY and VK_ADD instead of the regular keyboard character keys.

confidence.rationale: The current code path has a direct display-name collision and the symptom matches a save/load round-trip bug in the editor rather than a low-level injection failure.

issue_context.summary: A Keyboard Manager shortcut mapping that used to send numpad operator keys now saves as the regular keyboard characters in the new editor.
known_information: The report identifies version 0.100.2 and names Keyboard Manager as the affected area.
The affected mappings are Alt+8 -> numpad * and Alt+= -> numpad + on a laptop keyboard.
The issue is a regression from prior behavior and has no linked PR or assignee.
The automated triage comment marked reproduction as sufficient.
inferences: The low-level engine can inject distinct numpad-origin keys, so the higher-probability failure is the editor’s serialization path before the mapping reaches the engine.
The ambiguity is limited to keys whose display names collide; the existing dedicated labels for / and decimal explain why the report singles out * and +.
issue_context.analysis: This is ready for an implementation-grade design because the public report identifies a small failing surface, and the shared keyboard layout map exposes the exact place where the numpad operator identity can be lost.
initial_investigation: src/common/interop/keyboard_layout.cpp uses special labels for VK_DIVIDE and VK_DECIMAL but leaves VK_MULTIPLY and VK_ADD with layout-derived character names.
LayoutMap::GetKeyFromName() in src/common/interop/keyboard_layout.cpp returns the first matching display string from GetKeyNameList(false), so duplicate labels cannot round-trip safely.
KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Pages/MainPage.xaml.cs and KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Interop/KeyboardMappingService.cs both depend on GetKeyCodeFromName for shortcut save paths.

actions.label: Approve Keyboard Manager numpad-target design
actions.note: High-confidence fix centered on shared keyboard display-name round-tripping.

design.root_cause: Keyboard Manager’s shortcut editor stores selected keys by display name, then converts those names back to virtual-key codes through LayoutMap::GetKeyFromName(). In src/common/interop/keyboard_layout.cpp, VK_MULTIPLY and VK_ADD are left with the same display strings as the shifted main-keyboard characters "*" and "+", while GetKeyFromName() returns the first matching label it finds. That makes the round trip ambiguous and causes numpad operator targets to be saved as the wrong key code.
evidence: Observed: issue #50039 reports that shortcut targets meant to send numpad * and numpad + now send regular * and + in 0.100.2.
Observed: KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Pages/MainPage.xaml.cs builds saved shortcut strings by converting chosen key labels back into codes with GetKeyCodeFromName().
Observed: src/common/interop/keyboard_layout.cpp explicitly disambiguates "/ (Numpad)", ". (Numpad)", and numpad-origin navigation keys, but not VK_MULTIPLY or VK_ADD.
Observed: LayoutMap::GetKeyFromName() does a first-match scan over display names, so duplicate names cannot preserve numpad identity.
Inferred: because the regression is limited to the editor and operator targets, the most likely failure point is the editor round-trip rather than the runtime injection layer.

affected_files.purpose: Defines the canonical display names and reverse lookup used by the Keyboard Manager editor.
Declares the shared layout-map interface used by the editor interop layer.
Managed bridge that converts saved key names back into key codes for shortcut mappings.
Builds and persists shortcut mappings from the editor’s selected key names.
Existing managed test project suitable for save/reload and shortcut-editor regression coverage.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The layout map gives dedicated labels to some numpad-only keys but leaves VK_MULTIPLY and VK_ADD with plain character display names that collide with non-numpad keys.
implementation_steps.change: Assign unique labels to the numpad operator keys so the editor can distinguish them when users capture or pick them from the shortcut dropdown. Keep the labels human-readable and consistent with the existing numpad naming scheme.
edge_cases: Do not rename ordinary shifted character keys; only disambiguate the numpad operators.
Preserve current behavior for numpad-origin navigation aliases and saved mappings that already store numeric VK codes.
Check whether VK_SUBTRACT should be renamed to the same pattern for consistency without breaking any localized expectations.
tests: Enumerate the shortcut key list and verify the visible labels for VK_MULTIPLY and VK_ADD are unique.
Verify GetKeyDisplayName() returns the same unique labels when a key is captured from the hook instead of chosen from the dropdown.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Reverse lookup returns the first exact display-name match from the non-shortcut key list, so any duplicate label silently resolves to the wrong key.
implementation_steps.change: Keep the simple reverse lookup, but rely on the newly unique numpad labels and add a targeted regression assertion or helper to prevent future duplicate display names in the editor key list.
edge_cases: The shortcut list inserts a synthetic None entry; the uniqueness check must ignore that placeholder.

Locale-driven character names can still duplicate by keyboard layout, so the regression guard should focus on editor-selectable numpad operator entries rather than inventing a global uniqueness invariant for every printable key.
tests: Round-trip * (Numpad) and + (Numpad) through GetKeyDisplayName() -> GetKeyCodeFromName() and assert the result is VK_MULTIPLY / VK_ADD.
Confirm ordinary * and + character labels still resolve to the existing non-numpad keys.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Managed regression coverage focuses on remapping normalization and profile behavior, but it does not assert that shortcut-editor key labels round-trip to the intended numpad operator VKs.
implementation_steps.change: Add a focused editor regression that builds a shortcut mapping using the managed interop path, saves Alt+8 -> * (Numpad) and Alt+= -> + (Numpad), and verifies the stored TargetKeys use VK_MULTIPLY / VK_ADD and survive a reload.
edge_cases: Cover both dropdown selection and keyboard-capture display names if the test harness can access both paths.
Ensure the regression stays valid on layouts where the printable character for the top-row key is not literally the US "+" or "*" glyph.
tests: Run KeyboardManagerEditorUI unit tests covering the managed save path.
Perform a manual save/reopen check in the running Keyboard Manager editor on a layout without a physical numpad.

verify: Open Keyboard Manager, add Alt+8 -> * (Numpad) and Alt+= -> + (Numpad), save, reopen the editor, and confirm the same targets remain selected.
Use the saved mappings in a target app and confirm they emit numpad operators rather than the regular keyboard characters.
risks: Changing user-facing labels for numpad operators can affect saved-editor UX and any test baselines that expect the old text.
Locale-specific layouts may still produce other duplicate printable names; the fix should stay scoped to the confirmed numpad-operator regression instead of over-generalizing the entire key map.
alternatives: Carry numeric virtual-key codes through the editor UI instead of round-tripping display names. This is more robust long-term but changes a wider surface than the current regression needs.
Special-case VK_MULTIPLY and VK_ADD only in managed code. Rejected because the shared layout map is the canonical display-name source used by both old and new editor paths.
